headline: Tech sells off before Nvidia, crude slides as Hormuz traffic recovers, and rates stay the week's real story
lead: US stocks are on track for a broad down day: Nasdaq -2.5%, S&P 500 -2.0%, VIX up 24% to 23.9 late in the session.
Nvidia (-4.5% intraday) reports Tuesday, its first quarter since Jensen Huang stepped down; the board is reportedly not considering his return.
Rates are doing the heavy lifting: the US 2Y rose 42bp in five sessions to 4.88% and the 10Y sits at 5.15%. Wednesday's FOMC minutes should show how many officials leaned toward a hike.
Brent fell 3.7% to $92.29 and heating oil 6.2% as reports said Hormuz shipments keep recovering, even as a third US carrier arrived in the region and Tehran warned it may strike first.
Your Oil Monitor still shows Hormuz near-dark on transponders through Nov 8, so the recovery is in reported flows, not in visible ship counts.
Thursday brings the Anthropic IPO (range $70-78) and Philly Fed; OPEC+ meets Nov 29.

geopolitics.text: Tehran warned it may strike first if the US attacks again. The USS Theodore Roosevelt arrived in the region, making three US carriers in CENTCOM's area.
Bahrain said it intercepted Iranian aerial attacks after a nationwide threat alert on Sunday.
Foreign Minister Araghchi called for closer energy cooperation with regional producers and warned renewed US-Israeli strikes threaten stability. Iran and Pakistan also held talks.
Houthi forces are edging closer to Aden; sources put them within 80km as of Nov 2. They already hold the coast at Bab el-Mandeb.

Russian strikes killed three in Kherson, Dnipro and Zaporizhia regions. Zelenskyy says attacks on energy and heating infrastructure are intensifying before winter. Last week's Abu Dhabi talks produced a prisoner swap, no breakthrough.
The EU sanctioned nearly 50 banks and financial institutions plus people tied to Russia's oil and petroleum trade. Kallas accused Moscow of maximalist demands to prolong the war.

energy.text: Brent -3.7% to $92.29 and WTI -3.5% to $85.46 on the day, with Brent down 16% over a month. Prices fell as Hormuz shipments continued to recover.

Iranian output was 1.86m b/d in October, 46% below pre-war, with Iraq and the UAE adding 1.3m b/d. The IEA sees a Q4 surplus that widens in 2027, but onshore stocks are the lowest since at least 2016.
Heating oil fell 6.2% and RBOB 4.5% today; the 3-2-1 crack is about $40.57/bbl. European diesel was near $180/bbl in mid-November, about 77% above pre-war.
Seven producers including Saudi Arabia and Russia review output on Nov 29. They agreed on Nov 1 to hold September levels through December.

oil_monitor.summary: Hormuz is still near-dark on transponders and both Gulf chokepoints flag EXTREME. PortWatch counts ships with AIS switched on, not barrels, so this can diverge from reported flows. PortWatch data runs through Nov 8; Cushing is the EIA week of Nov 6.

markets.text: Nvidia fell 4.5% intraday after CNBC reported the board is not considering bringing Huang back, ahead of Tuesday's results. Consensus revenue is $109.1B.
US 2Y 4.88% and 10Y 5.15% at Friday's close, up 42bp and 31bp over five sessions. Wednesday's minutes from the Oct 27-28 FOMC should show how many of 19 participants leaned toward a hike.
The Philippine peso was the day's outlier: USD/PHP +1.4% to 63.85, a 3.8-sigma move for the pair. The dollar index is up 1.9% on the week.
Intel fell more than 6% after investors filed a class action. Europe closed modestly lower (DAX -0.6%, FTSE -0.2%).
